units.text: An online shop has a product photo to store. Where does the application put it, and how does it find it again? With Amazon S three, it puts the photo in a bucket. That bucket lives in one ay double-you ess Region, and the application asks for an object by its exact key.

The photo's key is images slash logo dot P N G. It looks like a file path, but the slash is part of one name. The object has the photo bytes, metadata such as its content type, and a storage class. Product photos, backups, and data lake files fit this way of working. But if the app needs mounted files or must update a disk in place, choose a file or block service before comparing S three storage classes.

The shop has saved its order. Now it wants a reporting app in another account to read it without exposing all its records. Start with the role running the app. Its identity policy can allow the read on that particular object. Then check the bucket or access point policy for permission from the resource side. An applicable explicit deny still wins.

What if another team uploaded the order? Bucket owner enforced makes the bucket owner own the uploaded object and turns off access control lists. That resolves who owns the object. It doesn't grant the reporting role permission to read it. If the request still gets Access Denied, check the principal, action, exact object, and effective policies. Fix the specific rule or missing permission rather than opening the whole bucket.
